subject: Day 23: confirm the 1-month visit is booked
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 23. The 1-month well visit window opens in five days. If it is not on the calendar, today is the day to call — popular pediatric slots fill a week or more out.

Action items
- Call and book the 1-month well visit now if it is not confirmed; target day 28-35. AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Assemble what to bring to the visit: the feeding log, the diaper-output log, and a written question list. AAP HealthyChildren overview of the first month: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Continue daycare or nanny tours; aim to have a shortlist with deposits down by the 1-month visit. Care.com: https://www.care.com/
- Order a second car-seat base if you have a second vehicle and have not yet. NHTSA car seat guidance: https://www.nhtsa.gov/equipment/car-seats-and-booster-seats
- Continue the feeding log.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cradle cap; blocked tear duct; brief head lifts and smoother movement.
- [low concern] First social smiles and sustained eye contact during alert windows.
- [monitor] Crying more than three hours a day on more than three days a week — the colic pattern peaking at six to eight weeks.
- [call within 24h] Forceful projectile vomiting with weight loss. Persistent inability to console with back-arching during feeds. Fewer than six wet diapers per day.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Keep tummy time at 15-20 minutes a day; tummy time correlates with earlier sitting and rolling. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Talk face-to-face 8-12 inches away to draw out an early social smile.
- Respond to every coo in a turn-taking rhythm. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Read aloud daily; the prosody of your voice is the active ingredient.

Upcoming
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit; first social smiles.
- Day 35-42: peak crying curve at about six weeks.
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit; first round of vaccines.
